transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-11-02 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~62m | Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Cortado Head of AI), Rahul Mehta (Platform Eng), Samir Khan (SRE)

Summary (auto): quick discovery to map Cortado's exit from OpenAI-hosted + vLLM internal stack -> evaluate Redwood hosted vs dedicated vs private. Key concerns: latency SLOs for chat product, KV cache compatibility, quantization differences, SOC2 and KMS, and migration cost. Agreement to run baseline parity eval and schedule on-prem perf testing.

[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): hey everyone thanks for taking the time, can you hear me ok?
[00:03] Lena (Cortado): yeah yes can hear it fine, thanks Maya. this is a discovery to see what it looks like to move off our current OpenAI + v L M combo into something a bit more predictable.
[00:12] Maya: great, quick intros please?
[00:15] Rahul: hi I'm Rahul, platform eng, I own infra and the deployment pipelines; we basically run a hybrid setup right now, some hosted OpenAI for rapid features and an internal vLLM cluster for cost-sensitive surface.
[00:26] Samir: Samir, SRE, i handle the GPUs, infra and uptime side, we have nightly outages we want to avoid.
[00:32] Diego (Redwood SE): Diego Ramos, infra/serving lead at Redwood, i'll be the technical partner for the evals.
[00:38] Maya: perfect. quick agenda: run through current stack, constraints, success criteria, privacy/compliance questions, then compatibility and baseline eval — ok?

[00:45] Lena: sounds good. current stack: user-facing chat product uses OpenAI for some high-complexity calls where hallucination tolerance is lower; lower-cost bursts and bulk inference go to our vLLM fleet (we call it v L M internally). We also use T G I for a couple of community models on preproc. main reasons to leave: cost unpredictability from hosted provider, and need for private VPC for regulated customers.

[01:10] Maya: can you quantify the usage? tokens per month, p95 latency SLO, concurrency?
[01:15] Rahul: rough numbers: 80M tokens/month across all endpoints, peak concurrency ~600 rps across roots, average generation length ~120 tokens. p95 latency target is 350-400ms for our short chat path, long path can be 900ms. also important: we need prefix KV cache support since we pre-warm prompts, and consistent top-p sampling behavior across model variants — we saw drift between local vLLM and hosted provider.

[01:45] Diego: when you say drift — is that output quality drift or tokenization differences?
[01:49] Lena: both, sometimes tied to tokenizer variants, sometimes quantization artifacts when we use 4-bit on vLLM. we want parity not exact but within our eval thresholds.

[01:58] Samir: and we have requirements around key management — customer data must be encrypted with our KMS, so any private or dedicated option needs to support BYOK or HSM integration.

[02:10] Maya: that's totally fair. Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS and on-prem packages; Dedicated can integrate with KMS in some setups, and Hosted we offer encrypted-at-rest but we know that's a blocker for some regs.

[02:24] Rahul: can you handle audit logs and SSO? we have to send logs to our SIEM and SSO is SAML.
[02:29] Diego: yes we have audit log sinks and SAML/SSO integrations, RBAC, and syslog export. i'll share the compliance doc after the call.

[02:38] [Speaker 1]: so from a performance perspective, what does the migration look like?
[02:42] Diego: few paths: 1) hosted API — lowest lift, good for non-sensitive traffic, best for quick feature parity; 2) Dedicated — reserved GPU pool with predictable throughput and commit pricing; 3) Private/on-prem — full VPC/on-prem option with customer-managed network and KMS. since you have existing vLLM, we often do a hybrid: keep the low-cost vLLM fleet for bulk and use Dedicated for latency-critical routes, with smart routing/fallback. that preserves cost while meeting SLOs.

[03:15] Lena: okay, tell me about vLLM compat — we use v L M for a lot of custom kernels and our infra is built around it. any surprises moving to Redwood runtime?
[03:24] Diego: our runtime supports common vLLM/TGI stacks but kernel differences can matter. we try to match attention kernels and KV cache behaviors; sometimes the transform codepath (TGI vs native) leads to small perf deltas. that's why we do a parity eval — we run your prompt set through both stacks and compare latency, token cost, and quality metrics.

[03:45] Rahul: what about quantization? we use 4-bit QAT in some models to save memory. can you run those?
[03:51] Diego: yes we have quantization support and profiles — 4-bit and int8 depending on model. we will surface quantization recommendations per workload; sometimes 4-bit changes output slightly, we'll flag that in the eval.

[04:04] Maya: can you walk through a sample timeline if we wanted to pilot next month?
[04:09] Diego: we typically do week 1: onboarding + access + prompt handoff; week 2: baseline eval (1k prompts) and perf runs; week 3: iterative tuning (batching, cache config, quantization profile); week 4: pilot and canary routing. on-prem runs require a bit more scheduling with your infra team.

[04:30] Samir: on-prem: what are the hardware footprints we should expect? GPUs per shard?
[04:34] Diego: depends on model family; for MPT-size-ish models one A100-80GB can handle X throughput — (note: numbers are approximate in transcript) but we'll produce a tailored sizing doc based on your traffic profile.

[04:46] Lena: security: SOC2, ISO? we need those docs for procurement.
[04:50] Maya: we are SOC2 compliant, have ISO in process; i'll send the SOC2 report and security packet after call (redwood.com/security.pdf).

[04:58] Rahul: we rely on OpenAI for some of the hallucination guardrails — are there builtin evals at request-level to detect quality regressions?
[05:04] Diego: yes, Redwood Optimize includes quality monitoring and regression alerts tied to prompt sets. we'll hook up your canonical test prompts and flag regressions pre-rollout.

[05:12] [crosstalk] Lena: okay good, how about pricing model for Dedicated — commit vs burst?
[05:17] Maya: Dedicated is commit-based monthly/annual with burst capacity for peaks. we'll send example scenarios: minimal commit for baseline throughput and incremental burst pricing.

[05:27] Samir: we have compliance customers that require traffic residency in EU only, is regional routing available?
[05:32] Diego: yes, routing by policy and region; Private deployments can be deployed in your VPC in the datacenter/region of choice.

[05:40] Lena: can we bring our own models? some of our customers train private fine-tunes.
[05:44] Diego: absolutely, model pinning and versioning are supported across hosted/dedicated/private. for private we give you more control over model artifacts.

[05:52] Rahul: one of our main technical fears: inference parity failures when moving from our vLLM pipeline to your runtime — what concrete steps reduce risk?
[05:59] Diego: run the parity eval first with your prompt set, measure exact metrics: latency distribution, token costs, sampling stats, and qualitative score through your annotators. if we see drift beyond thresholds, we iterate on quantization, kernel selection, and sometimes we recommend keeping certain routes on vLLM while routing others to Redwood. fallback policies keep your app online.

[06:23] Lena: what are typical speed differences? we've observed p95s on vLLM at ~320ms for short paths.
[06:28] Diego: for your workload we expect parity within 10-20% on latency after tuning; Dedicated typically improves consistency (less jitter) even if absolute median is similar. but again we'll instrument and share concrete numbers after the baseline.

[06:40] Maya: any blockers for moving existing OpenAI usage — e.g., API differences for function-calling or streaming?
[06:45] Diego: we support streaming, tool-calls/function-calling semantics similar to what's common; there are small differences in field names sometimes in the API surface, we'll provide a compatibility shim and migration guide for devs.

[06:58] Samir: procurement/legal will ask about data retention and deletion SLA.
[07:02] Maya: we have retention controls, customer-managed retention policies, and deletion APIs; we'll put that in the security pack.

[07:09] Lena: good. ok let's talk logistics — who will run the parity? do you expect us to provide prompts and reference labels?
[07:15] Diego: yes please provide the representative prompt set and a small labeled subset for quality checks. we'll run the 1k baseline on both your vLLM output and Redwood runtime and share the eval spreadsheet. Diego: i'll own the runner and spreadsheet.

[07:28] Rahul: timeline sounds tight — can we do the baseline in the next week?
[07:31] Maya: we can, assuming we get the prompt set and creds.

[07:34] [Speaker 2]: there's a question about cost modeling — how granular are the token and request breakdowns?
[07:39] Maya: Console shows token-level cost by route, per-model breakdowns, and you can get per-token cost attribution tied to customer tokens. Diego: plus we can simulate cost scenarios in the spreadsheet once we have your traffic mix.

[07:52] Lena: ok this has been really helpful. quick recap?
[07:55] Maya: recap: Redwood to send SOC2/security packet, Dedicated pricing samples, and a migration guide; Cortado to provide prompt set and traffic profile; Diego to run parity baseline and share the eval spreadsheet; schedule on-prem perf window next week.

[08:10] Rahul: agreed, i'll upload prompts to the shared folder and add the traffic CSV.
[08:14] Samir: i'll find a 2-hour block for the perf run and coordinate GPU access.
[08:18] Maya: perfect — i'll follow up with an email with links to docs and next steps.

[08:23] Lena: thanks everyone.
[08:25] Maya: thanks all, talk soon.

Artifacts referenced: security packet (redwood.com/security.pdf), parity eval template (drive.google.com/example-parity-spreadsheet), migration guide (docs.redwood.ai/migration-guide).

Notes on transcription: occasional speaker tag noise, "v L M" spelled out by transcript, "T G I" spacing, minor mis-hears around GPU sizing.

End of transcript.
